Summary: Over-voltage protection does not trip at exactly 4200 mV
Environment: Windows 11, GCC 16.1, Unity 2.6, host build with fake HAL
Description:
*Severity:* Critical - safety function fails at the specified limit
*Component:* Protection (firmware/src/bms.c)
*Affects version:* 1.0.0-dev    *Fix version:* 1.0.0
*Requirement:* REQ-BMS-010 (fault when any cell >= 4200 mV for 3 cycles)

h3. Steps to reproduce
# Start tools/bms_console.py
# @TICK 1
# @CELL 2 4200
# @TICK 3
# status

h3. Expected result
State FAULT, Faults 0x01 (OV), both FETs OFF

h3. Actual result
State IDLE, Faults 0x00, FETs ON. Unit test output:
{code}test_ov_trips_at_exactly_4200mV_after_3_cycles__REQ_BMS_010:FAIL: Expected 0x01 Was 0x00{code}

h3. Root cause
bms.c used vmax > BMS_OV_TRIP_MV instead of >=. The 4199 mV test passed - only the exact boundary exposes it.

h3. Resolution
Operator fixed. Retest passed; regression: 87 unit + 56 functional tests pass.

h3. Note
Seeded defect used to validate the test suite (defect seeding).

Summary: Test console crashes on non-ASCII input (UTF-8 BOM)
Description:
*Severity:* Minor - test tooling, workaround exists
*Component:* Tools (tools/bms_console.py)
*Affects version:* 1.0.0-dev    *Fix version:* 1.0.0

h3. Steps to reproduce
# Create input.txt containing PING
# Run: Get-Content input.txt | python tools/bms_console.py

h3. Expected result
OK,PONG is printed; invalid characters reported without ending the session

h3. Actual result
{code}UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode character '﻿' in position 0{code}
Session ends, transcript lost.

h3. Root cause
PowerShell 5.1 prefixes piped text with a BOM; the console did not handle non-ASCII input.

h3. Resolution
Leading BOM stripped, UnicodeEncodeError handled with a clear message. Retest passed.
